scqa.s: Accountingbpo is a Singapore professional services firm and business process outsourcing provider. It delivers tech-enabled financial management, corporate compliance and digital accounting workflows for client companies. The delivery model depends on two scarce resources: people who can read financial documents accurately, and people who can coordinate many client engagements at once. Both scale with volume, so growth historically meant hiring.
scqa.c: The award citation names three constraints. Manual data entry and reconciliation created heavy administrative work and delayed the completion of accounts. Assignments and client information were spread across separate documents, and coordination alone consumed about 400 hours each month. Higher client volumes therefore required more manpower, which capped scalability and compressed margins. The cost of growth was linear in headcount, and every additional engagement added coordination overhead before it added margin. The firm could not promise a faster turnaround without hiring, and hiring reduced the margin on the work that funded it.
scqa.q: How could the firm process more client documents and coordinate more engagements without adding proportional headcount, while keeping a qualified accountant's approval over every financial output?
scqa.a: The firm built Yi.Suite, an integrated ecosystem of specialised AI tools organised around its accounting workflow. Automated document processing extracts information from invoices, suggests ledger accounts and matches vendors, and handles both batch and single-document intake. A coordination layer converts client emails into trackable work tickets, recommends task assignments and drafts context-aware replies. Reconciliation matches bank transactions against accounting records and drafts receivables follow-up. Business owners can query financial data in plain language and receive KPI summaries and dashboards. Financial statement preparation compiles drafts and verifies documents, with accountants reviewing and approving the outputs. Human judgement stays at the approval boundary rather than at the data-entry boundary. The citation reports up to 67% less document processing time, up to 16 times faster management reporting, and 396 manhours a month redirected from coordination to client work. The citation does not report error rates, and it does not describe how the firm validates extraction accuracy, so the quality effect of the change remains unquantified. The reporting multiple is the more durable of the two speed figures, because management reporting is repeatable work with a fixed shape, while document processing time depends on the mix of client documents and will move as volumes change.

winners.takeaway: Automate the data entry, supervise the judgement. Put the accountant's approval after the AI's draft, not after the AI's extraction.

scqa.s: Best Marketing Agency provides digital marketing services in Singapore, including search engine optimisation, paid advertising, social media management and content creation. Agency economics depend on the ratio between billable output and the coordination required to produce it. Every additional client adds reporting, finance administration and internal handoffs before it adds margin.
scqa.c: Client delivery, reporting, finance and internal operations sat in separate tools, spreadsheets and chat threads. Account managers spent about two working days per client each month preparing reports alone. Finance and other administrative processes were also manual. The citation links manual coordination to high overheads and to senior staff being pulled away from sales, strategy and client engagement. The firm was paying specialist salaries for coordination work. Growth therefore added cost at roughly the same rate as revenue, which kept margin flat regardless of how many clients the agency won.
scqa.q: How could the agency raise output per person without lowering delivery quality or losing human control over client-facing and financial decisions?
scqa.a: The agency built Big Beast, an AI-powered operating system that connects delivery, reporting, finance and internal operations in one platform. AI agents execute routine processes, and human approval is retained for consequential actions. Automated reporting pulls advertising and search data, tracks keyword performance and generates campaign summaries and live reports. Finance workflows automate invoicing, bank reconciliation and accounting, with approval gates on financial actions. Operations bring task management, payroll, CPF computation, HR processes and contract e-signing together. Content agents draft search copy, advertisements and landing pages, with automated quality and compliance checks supporting human review. Lead routing, unanswered-enquiry flags and renewal-risk detection use campaign and payment records. The citation reports a 71% increase in revenue per employee, a 73% increase in delivery capacity per head, and 1,000 staff-hours saved from routine work each month. The company also publishes its own account of the award, which names Big Beast and describes a 24/7 AI salesperson for lead qualification. The citation does not separate the contribution of the agents from other changes in the period, so the 71% figure should be read as the firm's own account of the combined effect. Revenue per employee is the right headline here, because it captures both the hours removed and the work retained, whereas delivery capacity per head could rise simply by lowering the standard of what is delivered.

winners.takeaway: Measure revenue per employee, not tools deployed. The gain came from removing coordination work, not from drafting faster.

scqa.s: Blue Aqua International provides sustainable aquaculture, animal nutrition and farm management solutions to farmers worldwide. The Singapore Food Agency records that the company runs a local hatchery nurturing more than 100 million post-larval shrimp a year. Shrimp farming is a biological operation with thin margins: feed is a major cost, water conditions change faster than manual checks, and disease can spread through a pond before it is visible.
scqa.c: Water quality was checked infrequently, so problems could develop undetected between readings. Feeding was generic rather than matched to the pond, which wasted feed and money, and late disease detection raised the risk of stock loss. Decisions depended heavily on individual experience, paper logs and inconsistent records, which made performance hard to compare across farms. Expertise therefore did not scale: each farm's results depended on who was managing it. A farm manager's departure took the operating knowledge with them, and the company had no consistent way to compare one pond's performance against another.
scqa.q: How could the company convert scattered pond observations and individual experience into consistent, early warnings that any farm team could act on?
scqa.a: The company built AquaPilot, an aquaculture intelligence platform that analyses water quality, feeding, health and production data. Deployed across farm operations for approximately 1.5 years at the time of reporting, the system forecasts dissolved oxygen, ammonia and temperature six to 24 hours ahead using sensor and biological data, alerting teams to emerging water anomalies. It generates daily pond-level disease risk scores, delivering advance warnings four to seven days before health issues typically become visible. Feed calculations are pond-specific, dynamically weighing biomass, water conditions, growth trajectories and health risk. According to CEO Farshad Shishehchian in The Straits Times, this predictive feeding regime improved shrimp feeding efficiency by about 30%, adding operational specificity to the citation's broader 30% production cost management result. The system also monitors the recirculating aquaculture system, predicting equipment issues and adjusting feeding in response. A benchmarking layer compares ponds on feed conversion, survival, growth and cost, returning farm-specific recommendations. The published result is a 30% improvement in production cost management, survival rates 6 to 9 percentage points higher, and around 2,500 manpower hours saved each year. The survival-rate range is the more telling number, because it moves a biological outcome rather than a cost line, and biological outcomes are harder to attribute to any single management change than a feed bill is.

winners.takeaway: The model is the easy part. The value sits in turning sensor readings into a daily decision that a farm hand can act on before the loss happens.

scqa.s: GetGo Technologies runs an on-demand carsharing service on a pay-as-you-drive basis. A vendor case study published by Zendesk in 2024 records that the fleet exceeded 2,400 cars across more than 1,500 locations. Every rental begins and ends with photographs of the vehicle, taken by the customer. Those photographs are the only record of the vehicle's condition at the moment of handover.
scqa.c: The citation states that around 7,000 daily bookings generate about 56,000 end-trip photographs. Inspecting every booking manually is not feasible at that ratio. Damage could therefore go unnoticed until a customer reported it or a workshop found it days or weeks later. Late detection broke the link between damage and the booking that caused it, so the cost of repair could not be recovered from the responsible renter. The company carried the loss, and the invoice for damage arrived long after the rental ended. The company also carried the cost of disputes, because a charge raised weeks later is harder to defend than one raised at handover.
scqa.q: How could GetGo inspect tens of thousands of handover photographs a day, decide which booking caused any damage, and bill it accurately without accusing the wrong customer?
scqa.a: GetGo built Project Desmond, a damage detection system that combines computer vision, image matching and human validation. It analyses end-trip photographs and detects billable damage such as scratches, dents, cracks and dangling parts. It then compares consecutive bookings to establish when damage first appeared, and uses image embeddings to judge whether a detected defect is new or a recurring one already on file. Flagged cases route to human reviewers, who validate before any case proceeds to follow-up and billing. The model is retrained on real failure cases, including rain and reflections, to raise precision and cut false positives. The citation reports a 53% reduction in the lead time from damage to invoice, 60% less manual review work, and S$20,000 recovered in two months. The design keeps a person between the model and the customer, which matters when the output becomes a charge. The citation does not publish the model's precision or the dispute rate, so the commercial effect of a false positive is not documented. The recovered amount is a floor rather than a ceiling, because it measures only damage billed within two months, and says nothing about damage prevented, disputes avoided, or repairs found before a vehicle left the lot.

winners.takeaway: When AI output becomes a bill, the review step is not overhead. It is the control that makes the automation usable.

scqa.s: Glints provides talent and managed workforce services across Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, Vietnam, the Philippines and Taiwan. Its staff answer questions that cross borders: what a client was billed, which employee is assigned where, and what a given market's employment law requires. Each answer depends on a different system and a different jurisdiction.
scqa.c: Critical information sat across databases, business systems and the employment law of six markets. Routine questions needed help from Finance, Engineering or other specialists, and complex queries took hours or days. Repeated queries pulled specialists away from their own work. Worse, answers could differ between people and between markets, which created regulatory risk in an industry where an incorrect statement about pay or entitlement has consequences. The cost was not only time. It was the risk that two staff members would answer the same question differently in two markets.
scqa.q: How could staff get fast, consistent answers from company systems and six legal jurisdictions without queueing behind a specialist for every question?
scqa.a: Glints built Glimmer, a knowledge mining agent. Employees ask questions in plain language and the agent retrieves answers from company systems, internal knowledge, source code and employment law, showing the supporting sources. It pulls live client, employee, invoice and billing data from systems including NetSuite and HubSpot. It reads the company's source code to answer platform questions and provide first-line technical support before escalation. Governance is built into the retrieval: the system flags missing information, restricts citations to sources it actually accessed, and keeps audit logs. The citation reports a 90% reduction in fact-finding time, 1,700 specialist hours saved in six months, and S$120,000 of staff time saved each year. The design choice that matters is the citation constraint. An answer that must cite its source is auditable; an answer generated from general knowledge is not. The citation does not report how the agent handles a question that spans two jurisdictions, which is the hardest case in a six-market operation. The value of the agent compounds with market coverage, because every additional jurisdiction adds employment law that must be retrieved correctly rather than recalled from memory, and a wrong answer carries a regulatory cost.

winners.takeaway: Constrain the agent to sources it actually read, and log the retrieval. In a regulated service, an uncited answer is a liability, not a feature.

scqa.s: Greenphyto operates a high-density indoor vertical farm for large-scale crop production. The company opened a S$80 million facility in January 2026. Independent reporting describes a 23-metre growing structure, robots that place seedlings, and image analysis of plant height and leaf condition to track growth. Vertical farming compresses many growing layers into a small footprint, so a single undetected problem can affect a large share of output at once.
scqa.c: Plant defects and abnormal growth were not detected in time for intervention. Crop and equipment checks relied heavily on people working across multiple systems. Continuous crop measurement was limited, which made harvest planning difficult. In a stacked indoor farm, a person walking the racks sees a fraction of the crop at any moment, and the interval between inspections is the window in which a defect spreads. A defect found on a Tuesday walk-through had already affected the trays around it, and the cost appeared later as inconsistent yield rather than as a visible loss.
scqa.q: How could the farm inspect every growing layer continuously, catch defects earlier than a manual walk-through allows, and forecast harvest with enough confidence to plan supply?
scqa.a: Greenphyto built the AI-powered Farm Operations Management System, FOMS. It connects farm data, images, sensors and workflows into one system. Computer vision detects crop growth issues, defects and abnormalities earlier, and replaces many manual crop checks with image-based inspection. AI analysis of farm data improves yield forecasting, which supports harvest planning. Integrating farm systems, sensors and workflows reduces manual work, and real-time alerts flag problems such as lighting or device faults for follow-up. The published result is inspection ten times faster, a productivity improvement of up to 150 times, and 90% crop yield consistency. The company describes the platform as a fully integrated AI-driven autonomous farming system that lets operators farm without prior experience. Read plainly, the system moves the farm from periodic human observation to continuous machine observation, with people responding to exceptions. The citation does not state how many cameras cover the facility or how the model was trained, so the detection quality behind the tenfold figure is not documented. Yield consistency is the number that matters commercially, because a vertical farm's economics depend on predictable throughput across cycles rather than on peak output in a good one, and consistency is what buyers contract for.

winners.takeaway: In a stacked growing environment, the sensor grid is the business. Continuous observation is what makes both quality and harvest forecasting possible.

scqa.s: iAPPS Health Group provides primary care, preventive health and diagnostic services supported by proprietary digital health infrastructure. Its consumer brand, 1doc, operates a network of clinics and corporate health programmes. Third-party reporting in October 2025 recorded 9 own clinics and 21 affiliated clinics, more than 79,000 patients served and over 300 corporate clients. A clinic network of that shape generates administrative load faster than clinical revenue.
scqa.c: Pharmacy, claims and finance processes needed significant administrative resources as clinic operations grew. Patient records, pharmacy, claims, finance and workforce management sat in isolated systems. Workload was uneven and decision support was limited, which made it hard to expand while holding care quality constant. The constraint was not clinical demand. It was the administrative and coordination cost of serving each additional patient. Doctors absorbed the difference, which meant clinical time was being spent on administration rather than on patients.
scqa.q: How could the group expand clinic capacity without proportionally more administrative staff, while keeping doctors accountable for every clinical decision?
scqa.a: The group built 1docAI, described as an AI-native healthcare operating system. It connects six AI domains: patient care, clinical decision-making, health coaching, pharmacy, enterprise operations and payments. Patient management coordinates appointments, live queues and follow-ups. Clinical decision support retrieves source-linked clinical evidence, supports diagnostic reasoning and applies safety checks, with final decisions made by doctors. Health coaching uses longitudinal health data and behavioural signals to provide personalised coaching between consultations. Pharmacy and enterprise operations automate dispensing, inventory, claims, finance, reconciliation, HR and rostering. Clinical, operational and payment workflows share one longitudinal patient record. The published result is up to four times higher doctor productivity, up to ten times higher health coach productivity, and up to four times revenue growth across AI-enabled clinics. The design boundary is explicit: AI retrieves and drafts, the doctor decides. The citation does not publish clinical validation results, so the effect on diagnostic accuracy, as distinct from throughput, is not established. The coaching multiple is larger than the doctor multiple, which fits the design: coaching is routine guidance that a model can carry between consultations, while clinical judgement cannot be delegated without a governance answer.

winners.takeaway: Start with the record, not the model. A shared longitudinal record is what lets six AI domains serve one patient safely.

scqa.s: Kyanon Digital is a digital technology company and agile software development firm specialising in digital transformation, data analytics and enterprise IT. It delivers AI work for client organisations. A third-party report in April 2026 records that its Kyanon Consulting unit, formed in 2025, serves retail, banking and manufacturing clients. Consultancy economics depend on how much of each engagement is genuinely new work.
scqa.c: Teams rebuilt common capabilities for agent orchestration, retrieval, integrations, AI evaluation and monitoring before client-specific development could begin. Business rules were embedded in application code, so a routine rule change needed about five working days of engineering effort. AI quality checks depended heavily on manual review. The company could support around four concurrent AI engagements without adding senior AI engineers at the same rate. Demand could grow, but capacity could not, because each project started from zero. Senior engineers were therefore the constraint on revenue, and every new client competed for the same small group.
scqa.q: How could the firm stop rebuilding the same AI foundations on every engagement, and let non-engineers change business rules without a five-day code cycle?
scqa.a: Kyanon built WisdomMind, an enterprise AI platform that standardises core AI capabilities, business rules, integrations and quality controls. Teams start from a governed production framework and adapt it per client. A reusable foundation provides shared agent orchestration, retrieval, integrations and deployment. Governed business-rule management separates rules from application code, so authorised teams can update rules directly, with evaluation, versioning and approval applied before changes reach production. Automated quality evaluation tests AI changes against defined ground-truth scenarios and business rules before deployment, which catches regressions consistently rather than by inspection. Shared integration interfaces are built once and reused across agents and engagements. End-to-end monitoring tracks execution, latency, errors and inference cost. The citation reports 83% less setup time, business-rule changes 80 times faster, and 75% more concurrent delivery capacity. The citation does not report defect rates or client outcomes, so the platform's effect on delivery quality is not documented. The rule-change figure is the one that alters the commercial model, because it moves a task from engineering to operations without moving accountability, which is the difference between selling hours and selling a platform.

winners.takeaway: If every project rebuilds retrieval, evaluation and monitoring, you are not selling AI. You are selling repeated setup.

scqa.s: Limteh Project creates customised corporate gifts, gift sets and personalised presents. Each order carries customer-specific text, names, logos or artwork. The business runs on marketplaces and chat channels, so the personalisation instruction arrives as free text in whichever channel the customer used.
scqa.c: Personalisation details arrived through order notes, customer chats and messages, sometimes in different languages. Staff processed around 2,500 orders a month by hand, which created a daily production bottleneck. Order mistakes produced reprints, reshipping, wasted materials and unhappy customers. In a made-to-order business, an error found after printing cannot be corrected cheaply, because the material is already consumed. Staff time was also the constraint on customer service, because the same people answered enquiries, prepared production files and chased artwork approvals, so a busy week in production became a slow week for customers.
scqa.q: How could the company interpret thousands of free-text personalisation requests accurately enough to send straight to production, without a person retyping every order?
scqa.a: Limteh built Milo, an AI order automation system that carries personalised orders from sales to production. It reads orders and marketplace chats to identify each customer's personalisation requirements. It turns those requirements into production instructions and automates print-file preparation. A verification step cross-checks order details and flags uncertain orders for staff review, which keeps a person on the ambiguous cases rather than on every case. The system learns from staff corrections, so accuracy improves with use. Beyond production, it automates sales reporting, stock alerts, profit-and-loss dashboards and marketing content creation. The published result is 80% less rework on orders, more than 20 hours saved each week, and up to $5,800 saved monthly. The pattern is a narrow, high-value extraction task with a human exception queue, rather than a general assistant. The design also keeps a person on the ambiguous cases rather than on every case, which is what makes the throughput gain compatible with made-to-order accuracy at this volume. The monthly saving is small in absolute terms, which is precisely why it matters here: at this order volume the fix had to be cheap enough to justify itself quickly, and a large platform investment would not have paid back.

winners.takeaway: In made-to-order production, accuracy is cheaper than speed. Route uncertain orders to a person before the printer starts.

scqa.s: Lithan Academy provides adult education intended to bridge AI skills for the workforce. Its model is Competency Learning as a Service, which combines structured curricula with work-integrated learning. Course development is the production line: a module must map to competencies, carry content, assessments and rubrics, and survive quality review.
scqa.c: A 60-hour module required around 300 staff hours to map competencies and prepare content, assessments and rubrics. Learners progressed at different speeds, and limited trainer capacity made timely, customised support difficult. Attendance, assignments and programme progress were tracked separately, so learner problems surfaced late. The organisation was constrained at both ends: slow to produce a course, and slow to notice a learner falling behind. Both constraints hit the same budget line, so investment in course production competed directly with learner support.
scqa.q: How could the academy produce courses faster and support each learner individually, without diluting curriculum quality or losing trainer oversight?
scqa.a: Lithan built Adaptive CLaaS, an AI-powered personalised learning system in three modules. CLaaS Developer uses generative AI to draft learning pathways, session plans, content and assessments, with AI-assisted quality checks and curriculum teams reviewing and refining the output. CLaaS Mentor adjusts pace and difficulty based on learner progress and recommends resources for identified gaps, while providing on-demand guidance, reminders and automated assessment feedback, and escalating learners who need more support. CLaaS Manager consolidates enrolment, attendance, assignment completion and programme progress into a single view. The citation reports 75% faster curriculum development, 60% less manual monitoring and support, and about 60% year-on-year revenue growth. The human-in-the-loop boundary is explicit: AI handles repetitive drafting and routine guidance, while curriculum teams and trainers remain responsible for content quality and complex interventions. The citation does not report learning outcomes or completion rates, so the effect on educational quality, as distinct from production speed, is unmeasured. Revenue growth is the least attributable figure in the citation, because course production speed is one input among several, alongside demand for AI skills, pricing, and the sales capacity to fill the additional courses produced. Completion and pass rates would show whether faster production improved learning or merely accelerated it.

winners.takeaway: Generate the draft, not the decision. Curriculum teams kept authority over quality, which is what made the speed gain safe to sell.

scqa.s: Mencast Marine provides marine propulsion design, manufacturing and repair for the global marine and offshore industry. Its design work draws on decades of engineering and sea-trial data. The company competes in a market where lower-cost suppliers can replicate standard designs, so differentiation has to come from engineering judgement applied to a specific vessel.
scqa.c: Conventional design methods restricted the number of options engineers could evaluate, which slowed complex projects. Competition from lower-cost players compressed margins and put pressure on a design-led business. Production cycles were long, and manual information retrieval slowed quotations, claims processing and research. The constraint was not engineering capability. It was the number of design options a small team could explore, and the time spent finding information that already existed inside the company. Quotation delays cost orders in a market where the buyer is comparing several suppliers on response time.
scqa.q: How could a mid-sized propulsion designer evaluate far more design options per project and speed up quotation work, without hiring a larger engineering team?
scqa.a: Mencast built the Mencast AI Platform, MAIP, which combines AI, computer vision and enterprise knowledge automation. AI-powered propulsion design analyses thousands of design possibilities to identify higher-performing options and shortens the design process. Design differentiation uses decades of engineering and sea-trial data, so the firm can offer solutions beyond price competition. Intelligent manufacturing optimisation combines AI, computer vision and sensors to improve quality and support more efficient production. Enterprise knowledge automation organises company knowledge and automates workflows including quotations, claims processing, research and information retrieval. The published result is 50% faster design turnaround, 75% higher productivity on knowledge-intensive tasks, and $900,000 in new revenue within 18 months. The revenue figure matters more than the efficiency figures, because it shows the capability was sold, not only used internally. The citation does not state how design options are validated, so it is not clear whether the model replaces simulation or only ranks candidates for it. The revenue figure is the strongest evidence in the citation, because it is the only one that shows an external buyer paying for the capability, rather than the company measuring its own internal efficiency.

winners.takeaway: Point AI at the work you already charge for. Design exploration and quotation speed convert directly into won contracts.

scqa.s: Oceanus Media Global is a creative media technology company specialising in virtual production, generative AI, content production, distribution and IP licensing. Third-party coverage from 2023 describes its work in virtual and augmented production. The company's cost base is driven by where it films, not only by what it films.
scqa.c: Multi-location productions could take 14 to 15 weeks, because location scouting, permits, travel, set construction and filming run in sequence. Location fees, permits, travel, transport and set construction added significant cost. Crews and equipment were largely committed to one major production at a time, which capped the number of concurrent projects. The business was therefore limited by logistics rather than by creative capacity. Each location added a fixed cost that had to be recovered whether or not the shoot ran to schedule.
scqa.q: How could the company produce multi-location content without moving a crew to each location, and take on more projects with the same crew?
scqa.a: Oceanus built an AI-integrated virtual production pipeline that creates multiple locations virtually. It combines generative AI, computer vision and AI agents across pre-production, filming, post-production and localisation, with creative control retained by the team. Pre-production support covers script breakdown, scene planning, scheduling, storyboarding and visualisation. AI-generated virtual environments create digital sets and reconstruct real locations for filming in a controlled studio. Actors are filmed against those environments with real-time camera tracking maintaining correct perspective. AI-supported visual effects automate repetitive editing tasks and help build effects elements. Localisation supports dubbing in four languages and adapts approved content for different formats and platforms. The published result is around 80% shorter production timelines, up to 85% lower production costs, and a 200% increase in multi-location project capacity. The economics change because the studio becomes the location. The citation does not name the generation models or describe the studio hardware, so the technical basis of the 80% figure is not documented. A cost reduction of this size changes which briefs are viable, not only how profitably existing ones are delivered, because a client with a modest budget can now be offered a multi-location treatment that was previously out of reach.

winners.takeaway: Move the location into the studio, not the crew to the location. Fixed costs become reusable assets.

The firm describes its offer as a 360 solution, which means a single project draws on several disciplines and decades of accumulated precedent.
scqa.c: The citation reports that up to 2,750 manhours a week went into searching for project precedents, building regulations, policies and project information scattered across multiple systems. Technical expertise sat with experienced staff, and retrieving knowledge from past projects required knowing the exact reference to search for. Regulatory, design, presentation and financial reporting tasks were manual. The knowledge existed, but access depended on knowing who held it and what it was called. New staff took longer to become useful, and senior staff became a lookup service for their own archive.
scqa.q: How could the firm make twelve thousand past projects and Singapore's building regulations searchable in plain language, so that any staff member could find precedent without asking a senior colleague?
scqa.a: ONG&ONG built 360i, an AI platform that connects project knowledge, regulatory information and business workflows in a governed environment. Knowledge retrieval lets staff search over 12,000 historical projects and internal information using plain-language questions, with answers linked back to source records. Financial reporting consolidates and validates data across 10 entities to produce the group profit and loss statement, with AI analyst modules generating alerts, forecasts and scenario analyses. The platform extends into PowerPoint, Excel, Outlook and document workflows. The citation does not report retrieval accuracy or the proportion of answers that staff accepted without checking the source. The return figure is approximate, but the hours figure is the one a practice can test against its own timesheets before committing, which makes it the more useful number for another firm deciding whether to build the same thing.

scqa.s: Supreme Components International supplies active, passive and electromechanical components to original equipment manufacturers and electronics manufacturing companies. A distributor at this layer carries a wide franchise portfolio and competes on response speed and quoting accuracy. The work begins when a customer sends a request for quotation, often as an email with an attached spreadsheet or a PDF.
scqa.c: RFQs arrived in multiple formats and growing volumes, which made them difficult to process, track and manage. Manual product and brand matching increased the risk of quoting errors and caused avoidable follow-up. Supplier pricing and lead-time information was scattered across emails and records. Every quote therefore depended on a person assembling information from several places, and an error in part matching could produce a wrong price or a wrong lead time. Each avoidable follow-up consumed sales time twice: once to send the quote and again to correct it.
scqa.q: How could the distributor convert incoming RFQs of any format into structured, searchable requests and quote accurately without a person rebuilding the same information for every enquiry?
scqa.a: Supreme Components built Atlas, an AI RFQ-to-fulfilment platform. It extracts customer and product requirements from emails, PDFs, spreadsheets and other formats into structured data. Intelligent product matching matches requested products and brands against supplier information to streamline sourcing and quotation. Supplier intelligence extracts prices, inventory and lead times from emails, and identifies stock availability, supplier options and product alternatives. An automated workflow centralises RFQ and supplier information and automates supplier outreach, so information is easier to search, track and reuse. The published result is sourcing and quote preparation up to 90% faster, a 96% reduction in bills-of-materials preparation time, and up to $32,000 in monthly productivity gains. scqa.s: Thriving Weeds provides waste audits, data analysis and sustainability consultancy. Its clients need evidence of what they throw away, in what quantity, and how contaminated the waste streams are. That evidence usually underpins sustainability reporting and waste-reduction programmes. The company's own site describes AI- and IoT-enabled tracking for food waste segregation across multiple locations.
scqa.c: Conventional audits could involve six to eight people collecting and sorting waste for up to 12 hours a day. Short manual sampling periods made it hard to identify daily variation, repeated contamination or longer-term patterns. Repeated on-site audits and lengthy reporting required significant time for each premises. The result was a snapshot presented as a baseline, with the labour cost of producing it repeated for every site. Clients received a defensible snapshot, but not a trend, and the cost of the next snapshot was the same as the first.
scqa.q: How could the company measure waste continuously rather than in one exhausting sampling day, and do so across many premises without proportional labour?
scqa.a: Thriving Weeds built AuditEye, a waste-to-cloud ecosystem combining AI, IoT and cloud technology. Continuous monitoring captures disposal records throughout the deployment period, producing a larger and more representative dataset. AI-enabled contaminant detection identifies contaminants in waste streams and records when contamination occurs, including disposal weight and frequency. Automated data capture links images with weight, time, location and waste-stream information to create standardised records. Cloud processing handles records in near real time and provides access to waste data, images and downloadable records. Human-validated analysis combines continuous monitoring with consultant review and physical audits. The published result is 60% fewer flagged contamination incidents, more than 95% accuracy in waste weight measurement, and up to 384 manhours saved per audit. The company retains human verification and professional consultancy for recommendations, which keeps the output defensible. The citation does not describe the hardware or the reference method used to establish the 95% accuracy figure. The contamination figure is the commercial one, because clients buy a reduction in incidents rather than the accuracy of the measurement behind it, though the accuracy figure is what makes the incident count defensible in a report.

winners.takeaway: Continuous measurement beats a heroic sampling day. A longer, lighter dataset is both cheaper and more credible.

scqa.s: Agape CP Holdings is a social enterprise providing contact centre, customer experience, business process outsourcing, recruitment and workforce development services. Its output is measured in handled interactions, and its cost base is agent time. In a contact centre, the minutes after a call are as expensive as the call itself, because they are paid for but not billable to the customer.
scqa.c: Agents spent three to five minutes documenting each interaction and updating records, which reduced the time available to serve customers. Supervisors could review only about 5% of interactions, so service gaps, compliance risks and coaching opportunities went unseen in the other 95%. New agents took around six weeks to reach independent productivity, and some needed extra knowledge support and coaching during initial deployment. The operation was therefore limited by documentation load and by the thin sample of quality review. Coaching therefore relied on anecdote, because the sample rarely contained the interactions that caused problems.
scqa.q: How could the contact centre reduce post-call administration and review far more interactions for quality, without adding supervisors or slowing onboarding?
scqa.a: Agape built an AI-powered contact centre and BPO platform that combines generative AI, speech analytics and workflow automation. During live calls, agents receive real-time caller sentiment analysis and customer profiles synthesized from past calls, helping them assess caller emotions and de-escalate difficult conversations on the spot. The platform provides real-time guidance, suggested responses and instant access to relevant standard operating procedures and campaign information without searching through documents. Automated documentation transcribes conversations and generates interaction notes, structured summaries and email follow-up drafts, removing three to five minutes of repetitive post-call administrative work per call. Quality assurance analyses interactions at scale to identify service gaps, compliance risks, sentiment trends and specific coaching opportunities, expanding supervision from a 5% sample to near-complete coverage. New employees receive live prompts and standardised knowledge, shortening the path to independent work. The published result is 63% less time on administrative tasks, 33% faster onboarding, and 16 times more quality assurance coverage. The quality coverage figure is the more interesting one, because it changes supervision from sampling to census, converting quality assurance from an ad hoc check into an auditable control that regulated outsourcing clients require.

winners.takeaway: Automate the note-taking, then use the transcript you now own. Full coverage of interactions is a supervision capability, not a reporting nicety.

scqa.s: Brew Interactive provides lead generation, performance marketing, search engine optimisation, Generative Engine Optimisation and marketing automation. The agency's product is speed of testing: the faster it can produce and test creative, the faster it learns what works for a client. Its constraints are therefore handover friction and production latency.
scqa.c: Handover documents for new clients took three to four hours to prepare, with a risk of information gaps between the sales and delivery teams. Research, strategy development, content drafting and client communications required significant effort. Video production could take two to three weeks, which limited the speed and variety of creative testing. The agency could not test more concepts without either more production capacity or a longer schedule. Producing a video was therefore a scheduling decision as much as a creative one, and the agency could not promise a client a fast test cycle when its supplier was busy with another account.
scqa.q: How could the agency shorten onboarding and video production enough to test more creative per client, without hiring a production team?
scqa.a: Brew Interactive embedded a named set of AI tools across sales, operations and creative workflows. MeetGeek transcribes client meetings while Claude generates structured handover documents, which replaces the manual three to four hour write-up. Claude also assists with research, strategy development, content drafting and client communications. Higgsfield generates AI video assets, and AdCreative.ai generates advertising creatives, which removes most of the two to three week video cycle. Blip AI supports routine written communications across departments. The published result is 85% faster onboarding, about 85% less time producing videos, and up to $10,000 saved monthly on creative production. This is the clearest vendor disclosure among the thirty winners: the citation names each tool and the task it performs, which makes the implementation reproducible by another agency. The stack is also the most completely disclosed in the set, which makes it the easiest implementation to replicate and the easiest to cost before committing budget. The video figure matters most for an agency, because production latency is what limits how many creative concepts a client can afford to test, and testing volume is usually the constraint on performance improvement.

winners.takeaway: Name the tool and the task it does. A stack you can describe is a stack another team can copy.

scqa.s: Catalyst Performance is a personal training studio at Manulife Tower in Singapore's central business district. Bervin Manoharan, Jeremy Soh and Dr Luqman Haris founded it after corporate careers in the industry, and their coaching experience spans more than 25 years combined. The studio coaches working adults from their thirties onward, including clients over 50, athletes, and pre-natal and post-natal clients. Every client starts with a four-pillar Healthspan Assessment covering body composition, cardiorespiratory fitness, stability and strength. It is a small business with a small team, competing for local attention against larger gyms that employ marketing departments.
scqa.c: The legacy website lacked search engine optimisation and generative engine optimisation infrastructure, and the studio sat on page four of Google. Website updates, content creation, advertising campaigns and lead outreach required significant time or external agency support, and the studio had no in-house digital capacity for any of it. Manoharan states that there was budget for an agency, but that no agency would promise an outcome, so the work was taken on internally instead. Growth therefore depended on buying attention or on the founders' spare hours. Marketing was intermittent, which is the worst pattern for search visibility, because gains decay when publishing stops.
scqa.q: How could a small coaching business build and run a full digital acquisition operation, and own the systems behind it, without hiring an agency or a technical team?
scqa.a: Manoharan built the systems himself: the website, the marketing systems, the operations panel, the WhatsApp and Instagram assistants, and the client nutrition log. Each is built around how the studio coaches, and each uses whichever model does the job best. The company release names DeepSeek and Fable, describing the latter as the latest Claude model from Anthropic. The rebuilt website carries search and generative engine optimisation infrastructure. Automated outreach powers LinkedIn messaging, email campaigns and personalised follow-ups. Advertising analysis reviews Meta, Google and TikTok campaign data to find inefficient spend, and AI-operated dashboards report bookings, leads, protocol sales, email performance and funnel analytics. The published result at nomination was more than 300% more organic search clicks, a 190% increase in impressions and more than double the Google ranking. The Singapore Business Federation checked the nomination figures at the studio in August. The stated next step is ownership, with capital going into hosting the studio's own models and infrastructure so that processing sits inside the business.

winners.takeaway: Owning the stack is the difference between renting a capability and holding one. The gain is not the model; it is that nobody else can switch it off.

scqa.s: GOODSTUPH provides creative media and social marketing services. Its work is campaign-led: a client brief becomes a concept, then a production, then a set of assets for several platforms. The agency's margin depends on how much of that chain it controls and how many concepts it can afford to test.
scqa.c: External shoots, studios and post-production accounted for roughly 60% of total expenses in the first half of 2025. External production added two to four weeks to a typical campaign, and changes could add another three to five days. High production costs limited the number of concepts the agency could test, and made some lower-budget briefs uneconomical to serve. The agency was paying a third party for the capacity to experiment. Every concept the agency did not test was a decision made by budget rather than by judgement.
scqa.q: How could the agency produce campaign creative in-house, fast enough to test more concepts, without losing the creative judgement that clients pay for?
scqa.a: GOODSTUPH built AI.YAH, a generative AI creative production system that combines large language models, image generation and generative video within a structured creative workflow. Language models develop creative concepts and scripts. Generative image and video production creates images, videos and creative variations in-house, which reduces reliance on external shoots and post-production. Role-based prompt frameworks guide output against defined creative and quality standards, so results are repeatable rather than improvised. Human creatives direct the process, evaluate outputs and retain final approval. The published result is more than 30% cost savings, up to four times faster production, and over 200% more creative output. The citation reports campaign production falling from four weeks to seven days. The structural change is that production capacity became a fixed internal cost rather than a variable external one, which is what makes testing more concepts affordable. The citation does not name the generation models, and it does not report client approval or rejection rates for generated work. The output increase is the strategic figure, because it changes how many concepts the agency can put in front of a client within one budget, which affects win rates more than a marginal reduction in cost per asset.

winners.takeaway: The cost saving is the smaller story. In-house generative production turns creative testing from a budget decision into a routine.

scqa.s: iHub Solutions provides technology-enabled logistics, including smart warehousing, e-commerce fulfilment and last-mile delivery. Its customers need answers about their own stock: what is where, how much moved, and when it will arrive. The company runs a Warehouse Management System, and its public materials describe a Virtual Logistics System deployed across Singapore, Malaysia, Hong Kong and Thailand.
scqa.c: Ad hoc data requests required manual extraction, manipulation and report creation beyond the standard system reports. Complex requests needed software developers to write SQL queries against the underlying database. Customer service and software development teams spent about 25 employee-hours a day responding to reporting and data requests. Developers were therefore doing reporting work instead of building, and customers waited for answers that the system already held. Customers experienced the delay as poor service, even though the data existed and was accurate.
scqa.q: How could customers and staff get answers from warehouse data in plain language, without a developer writing a query for each request?
scqa.a: iHub built Gideon, a generative AI virtual assistant that uses natural-language conversation to make warehouse and delivery data accessible. Users ask questions in plain language instead of searching reports or understanding database structure. The assistant converts requests into SQL queries and retrieves data directly from the Warehouse Management System. It generates charts, refines queries through conversation and presents results in a readable format. Self-service analytics lets customers and non-technical employees reach operational insight without the technical teams. The published result is $94,500 in projected annual cost savings, 60% less time handling data requests, and 15 hours saved per day. The critical design choice is that the assistant queries the system of record rather than a copy, which keeps the answer current but puts weight on query safety and access control. The citation does not describe how customer-level access is enforced, which is the main risk in exposing a shared warehouse database. The daily hours figure is more meaningful than the annual saving, because it describes capacity returned to the development team, and that capacity is what a logistics operator would otherwise have to buy in. The saving recurs monthly, which is what makes it worth engineering rather than buying as a one-off.

winners.takeaway: Text-to-SQL works when the schema is yours and the permissions already exist. Point the assistant at the system of record, not a stale extract.

scqa.s: Innovative Hub (SG) offers digital marketing and e-commerce services to clients across Singapore, Malaysia and Vietnam. The work is proposal-led and multilingual: a client asks for a scope, the team drafts a response, and content must then be localised for several markets. Three countries mean three time zones and several languages.
scqa.c: Proposal drafting and compliance checks required significant manual effort. Customer response and content translation depended on specialist availability and were limited by time zones. Business growth depended on hiring more staff to handle increasing workload. A request that arrived after a specialist's working day waited until the next one, and every new client added proposal and compliance work before it added revenue. Compliance review was the step most exposed to that delay, because it sat at the end of the process.
scqa.q: How could the agency respond to clients across three markets without adding staff for every increment of volume, while keeping compliance checks intact?
scqa.a: Innovative Hub embedded AI tools including Claude, ChatGPT and OpenMax across daily workflows to automate routine tasks, retrieve data and respond to clients quickly. Proposal turnaround fell from a full day to a few hours. Content localisation and translation complete within the same day rather than waiting on a specialist in another time zone. Automated compliance streamlines audits, checklists and sensitive-word checks. Cross-platform task support lets the tools work across messaging platforms, spreadsheets and internal databases on multi-step tasks. The automation extends to prospecting, HR triage, morning briefings, reporting and client monitoring. The published result is twice the employee productivity, 75% faster customer response and 80% faster proposal creation. The compliance automation is the part worth copying: in a multilingual agency, sensitive-word checks are the step most likely to be skipped under deadline pressure, and the step most likely to cause a problem. The citation does not report the false-positive rate of the sensitive-word checks, so the review burden they create is unknown. The compliance automation is the part that protects the speed gain, because faster proposals without a checking step would simply move risk downstream to the client relationship and the contract. The ordering matters more than the tools chosen, because a check after the draft is what makes speed safe.

winners.takeaway: Automate the compliance check, not only the draft. It is the task people skip when they are busy, and the one that creates liability.

scqa.s: Kopi Near Me operates a network of automated coffee vending machines across commercial, healthcare and transport locations in Singapore. The business is a field operation disguised as a retail one: every machine needs replenishment, cleaning and repair, and every site has different access rules and demand patterns. Revenue depends on machines being available and stocked.
scqa.c: Customer requirements arrived through multiple communication channels, and staff had to extract the information manually and prepare sales documents. Managing replenishment, maintenance and repairs across machines required extensive coordination of technicians, routes and operational priorities. Inventory, logistics and operational records sat across multiple systems and spreadsheets, which meant manual data entry and limited visibility. The company could see sales, but not the operational state that produced them. A machine could be sold out and broken on the same day without either fact reaching the person planning tomorrow's route.
scqa.q: How could the operator schedule technicians and stock across a growing machine network without a coordinator rebuilding the plan by hand each day?
scqa.a: Kopi Near Me built an AI-enabled operating system that automates sales, scheduling and operational workflows. The sales component extracts customer requirements from enquiries and converts them into structured sales orders, quotations and contracts. Dynamic scheduling and routing optimise replenishment, maintenance and repair schedules, and adjust technician deployment as operational needs change. A centralised operations layer manages inventory, logistics and operational records in one platform, which reduces manual administration. Real-time dashboards give management live operational visibility for planning. The published result is up to 15% higher sales conversion, a 70% reduction in manual enquiry processing, and 80% less time on technician scheduling. The interesting number is conversion: enquiry handling speed affects revenue directly in a business where a site manager is comparing suppliers. The citation does not report stock-out or machine-uptime figures, so the operational effect of scheduling is not quantified. Conversion is the figure to watch, because scheduling and stock accuracy reach the customer as machine availability, and availability is the thing a site manager is actually buying when comparing suppliers. Uptime and stock-out rates would be the next figures to publish, because they show whether availability improved.

winners.takeaway: Scheduling is the product in a field-service business. Optimise the route and the machine is available when the customer wants coffee.

scqa.s: McLink Asia provides office equipment, enterprise software integration and managed IT services to businesses in Singapore and Asia. Its marketing function supports a portfolio of products and services sold through partners. The company is not a marketing agency, so campaign production competes with delivery work for the same staff.
scqa.c: Staff took hours or days to respond to social media enquiries. A single campaign required eight to twelve hours of combined staff effort to deliver. Manual revisions and handovers slowed production further, which limited the ability to respond to market opportunities. The pattern is familiar in small B2B firms: demand arrives through social channels, but nobody owns the response because everyone has a delivery deadline. Response delay is expensive in social selling, because the first supplier to reply usually sets the shortlist, and a late answer is often no answer at all.
scqa.q: How could the company respond to enquiries within minutes and produce campaigns with the same headcount, without hiring a marketing team?
scqa.a: McLink Asia built a multi-agent AI marketing platform that automates marketing from lead qualification to reporting. Specialised agents qualify leads by responding to social enquiries, generate content including blogs, newsletters, videos and promotional images, and prepare campaigns for distribution. The agents work across campaign tasks, which removes the manual handovers that caused delay. Automated marketing analytics collects advertising data and prepares performance reports with less manual work. The published result is a 200% increase in campaign production capacity, 95% faster customer response, and 85% faster campaign roll-out. The architecture is the point: separate agents for qualification, content and analytics, rather than one general assistant, so each step can be tuned and evaluated on its own. The architecture separates qualification, content and reporting so that each step can be evaluated, tuned and replaced without rebuilding the others, which is the practical advantage of splitting agents by role rather than deploying one general assistant across the whole function. Response speed is the figure with a direct commercial consequence, because a slow reply in social selling usually means a lost shortlist place, and no amount of additional campaign output recovers a lead that went elsewhere.

winners.takeaway: Split the work into roles before you add agents. Specialised agents are easier to evaluate than one general assistant.

Its administration is a scheduling problem with a customer service surface: students reschedule, teachers have availability, and invoices recur. The school's communication channel is WhatsApp, because that is where its students already are.
scqa.c: Two administrators spent around 60 hours each week managing messages, schedules and reminders, which reduced the time available for other work. The school was paying two people to relay messages between a calendar and a chat app. After-hours requests waited, which is exactly when working adults tend to reschedule.
scqa.q: How could the school resolve scheduling requests within minutes at any hour, reduce no-shows, and collect fees on time, without adding administrative staff?

It sends lesson and invoice reminders, marks attendance, generates invoices and extends recurring lesson series. Staff get a single view of conversations with AI-generated summaries and can take over at any point. Billing matters, complaints and complex requests route to staff for review. Messages handled per administrator is the figure to watch next, because it caps how far the model scales.

scqa.s: The Gourmet Factor operates and manages restaurant brands across several dining concepts. Multi-concept restaurant groups carry a specific cost problem: each outlet has its own stock, its own suppliers and its own menu, but the group needs a single view of margin. Food cost is the largest controllable cost line in a restaurant.
scqa.c: Stocktaking and supplier invoice processing required significant staff effort, which reduced time for higher-value work. Fragmented stock records reduced visibility into inventory levels and contributed to shortages, over-ordering and excess stock. Supplier pricing sat buried in unprocessed invoices, which made accurate menu costing difficult and slowed the response to cost increases. The group could not see whether a dish was profitable until well after the ingredients were consumed. Menu pricing was therefore set on last quarter's costs, which is a slow way to react to a supplier increase.
scqa.q: How could the group know the true cost of each menu item as supplier prices changed, without adding finance staff to key in invoices?

Automated invoice processing extracts supplier invoice details using optical character recognition and machine learning, which reduces manual data entry. Digital stocktaking captures inventory counts on mobile devices and synchronises stock across locations. Real-time recipe costing updates dish costs using live supplier prices, which gives visibility into menu-item margins. Purchasing decisions draw on inventory and costing data to reduce shortages, over-ordering and excess stock. The published result is 100% return on investment within five months, 80% faster invoice processing and 40% less time on stocktaking. The vendor is named in the citation, and its own product site describes AI-powered restaurant management, so the implementation is unusually well documented for an adoption winner. The citation does not report the size of the group or the number of invoices processed monthly. Payback within five months is the figure a restaurant group will test first, because food cost changes arrive monthly and any tool that takes a year to pay for itself will be judged against a very short operating horizon.

scqa.s: TTS Group provides transport planning, traffic engineering and transport analytics consultancy. Its clients are road authorities and developers who need evidence about how a junction or corridor behaves. The company's public materials describe AI-powered intelligent transport systems analytics within its portfolio. The core input is video of traffic, and the core output is a defensible assessment of risk.
scqa.c: Surveyors manually counted and classified vehicles and pedestrians, which required multiple personnel and extended shifts at high-volume sites. Engineers spent around 15 hours a week reviewing footage for a single intersection, which capped the number of sites the firm could assess. Assessment was reactive, because periodic observation and historical crash data make it difficult to detect near-misses and identify risk before an incident. A near-miss is, by definition, an event that does not appear in crash statistics. Waiting for collisions to accumulate means the evidence arrives only after the harm.
scqa.q: How could the firm analyse far more junctions without proportionally more surveyors and engineers, and detect risk before a collision occurs?
scqa.a: TTS Group built a proactive framework for near-miss-based traffic risk assessment. Computer vision detects, tracks and classifies vehicles and pedestrians, which reduces reliance on manual counting. Movement-pattern analysis identifies traffic conflicts that do not appear in conventional crash-based assessments. Traffic and near-miss data quantify risk and rank locations. AI-assisted intervention planning synthesises data from high-risk intersections to support targeted measures such as signal optimisation. Continuous post-intervention monitoring reassesses sites to measure change in safety risk and compare before and after. Engineers retain responsibility for safety recommendations. The published result is about a 98% increase in traffic-data acquisition capacity, about 30 hours saved per engineer each week, and roughly 50 times more sites processed monthly. The near-miss method is the substantive change: it shifts the evidence base from what happened to what nearly happened. The citation does not publish validation of the near-miss metric against observed crash frequency. The sites-processed figure is the strategic one, because it changes the unit of analysis from individual junctions to a network, and a network view is what makes proactive safety spending defensible to a road authority.

winners.takeaway: Change the unit of evidence. Near-misses are more frequent than crashes, so they produce a usable sample before anyone is hurt.

scqa.s: You Tiao Man manufactures traditional Asian snacks and frozen dough fritters, supplying hotels, restaurants, caterers and supermarkets. It is a food manufacturer with a distribution business attached: production is planned, but orders arrive through several sales channels and suppliers invoice against deliveries. The administrative load sits between the factory and the customer.
scqa.c: Orders arrived through multiple sales channels, and staff had to capture and consolidate information across systems by hand. Supplier invoices were manually entered, validated and reconciled across spreadsheets and finance systems. Payment tracking, follow-up and repetitive order administration reduced the time available for business development and customer engagement. In a low-margin food business, administration is not overhead that can be absorbed. It is margin. The work also fell on the same small team that handles sales, so administration displaced revenue-generating activity.
scqa.q: How could a food manufacturer with no engineering team automate order, invoice and finance administration without replacing its existing systems?
scqa.a: You Tiao Man built an AI operations co-pilot using n8n and Claude. It integrates with existing business systems to reduce manual processing while keeping staff in control of approvals. Invoice processing extracts invoice details, validates pricing against master records and flags discrepancies for staff review. Automated finance workflows maintain payment records and transfer approved invoice information into finance systems, which reduces duplicate entry and reconciliation. Multi-channel order visibility consolidates orders into a live dashboard showing revenue, orders and outstanding actions. AI-assisted marketing researches and drafts social media content, checks it against company policies and routes posts for approval. The published result is 85% return on investment within the first year, 83% less time processing invoices and 40 manhours saved per week. This is the most reproducible implementation in the set: a named orchestration tool and a named model, applied to ordinary back-office work. The citation does not report the exception rate or how often invoices require manual correction. The exception rate, which the citation does not publish, will decide whether the saving holds as invoice volume grows, because every exception returns work to the same small team that the automation was meant to release. Volume is the real test, because the workflow has to hold when invoice count doubles.

winners.takeaway: You do not need a platform team. A workflow tool and a model, pointed at invoices and orders, is enough to change a small manufacturer's week.
